solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Regulatory device sees mother recycling, say, no end

indicators.note: recycled material is broken down and remade in a fresh form, so the word's letters get reworked
having no end means the final letter of the preceding word is dropped

parts.note: to state something is to say it

explanation.surface: A household gadget watches Mum diligently sorting the recycling.
explanation.walkthrough: Mother rearranged gives THERMO, and STATE losing its last letter gives STAT.
explanation.definitionFit: A thermostat switches heating on and off to keep temperature steady, so it is a device that regulates.

clue.text: Performer's act of kindness

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a stage act in a variety show
second meaning: a good deed, as in doing someone a good one

explanation.surface: An entertainer's routine turns out to be a charitable gesture.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as one phrase, 'act of kindness', but it splits into a music-hall act and the 'good ...' of a favour done.
explanation.definitionFit: A variety performer's slot on the bill is called this, and a favour is a 'good' one of these in the idiom.

clue.text: Order red wine? Do, it may keep us warm

indicators.note: to order things is to put them into a new arrangement, so the following letters are sorted afresh

explanation.surface: Someone urges ordering a glass of red because it will warm us up.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests mulled or red wine as the warming thing; the warmth comes from a quilt.
explanation.definitionFit: An eiderdown is a thick quilt filled with duck down, laid on a bed for warmth.

clue.text: Good quality, charmer, Italian, shows

indicators.note: the words display the target on view inside them, spanning the gap between two of them

parts.note: the end of charmer runs into the start of Italian

explanation.surface: A charming Italian man displays a fine character.
explanation.definitionFit: Merit is worth or excellence, a good quality that deserves praise.

clue.text: Type of card, rail, new, not very different

parts.note: a SIM card goes in a mobile phone

indicators.note: making something new means remaking it, so the preceding word's letters are recast

explanation.surface: A list of things that look alike: a card, a rail, all quite the same.
explanation.definitionFit: Similar things resemble each other closely, so they are alike rather than greatly unlike.

clue.text: After broadcast, decline delivery

parts.note: to air a programme is to broadcast it
a drop is a fall or decline

explanation.surface: Once a show goes out, its viewing figures fall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' just sets the order: the first piece comes before the second.
explanation.definitionFit: An air-drop is the delivery of supplies by parachute from an aircraft.

clue.text: As outsiders leave, orphan playing instrument

indicators.note: the outsiders of a word are its first and last letters, and they leave
playing about with letters means moving them around into another order

parts.note: orphan with its first and last letters removed

explanation.surface: A lonely orphan plays music as the strangers depart.
explanation.definitionFit: A harp is a large stringed instrument plucked with the fingers.

clue.text: Fighter in from France, unfamiliar

explanation.surface: A boxer has arrived from France, and he is a stranger here.
explanation.definitionFit: Alien as an adjective means strange or foreign, not known to one.

clue.text: Nice fellow maybe welcoming romantic meeting in flat

indicators.note: a host welcoming a guest takes them inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: a typical French man's name, Nice being a city in France
a date is a romantic appointment

explanation.surface: A pleasant man invites a romantic encounter at his apartment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nice' is the French Riviera city, not the adjective, so the fellow is a Frenchman with a typical French name.
explanation.definitionFit: A pied-à-terre is a small flat kept for occasional stays, typically in a city away from one's main home.

clue.text: Attractive publication — bring up quote, fun ultimately

indicators.note: in a down clue, bringing up means reading upwards, so the order flips
ultimately points to what comes at the very end, so the last letter is kept

explanation.surface: An appealing magazine dredges up a funny line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bring up' covers both the quote and the last letter of fun, flipping them as one unit.
explanation.definitionFit: Magnetic describes a person or thing with a strong pull, so it is a synonym for attractive.

clue.text: Jockey's extra stipulation

definitions.meaning: first meaning: someone mounted on a horse
second meaning: a clause added to a contract or bill

explanation.surface: A horseman has an additional condition in his contract.
explanation.walkthrough: The possessive reads as 'is', linking two separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: A jockey rides horses in races, and a clause tacked onto a document is also called by this name.

clue.text: Forces member passing over retrograde newspaper's spread

indicators.note: a piece passing over another stretches across it, ending up on both sides of it

parts.note: a marine is a soldier serving with a navy

indicators.note: retrograde means moving backwards, so the word is read from end to start

parts.note: a rag is a disparaging word for a newspaper

explanation.surface: A soldier skips past a backward-looking newspaper's coverage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spread' looks like a newspaper layout but is the definition: something you put on toast.
explanation.definitionFit: Margarine is a butter substitute, something spread on bread.

clue.text: One talking foolishly in image promotion about toy

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece wraps round the other

parts.note: public relations, which promotes an image
a baby's toy that makes a noise when shaken

explanation.surface: A babbling spokesperson runs a publicity campaign for a toy.
explanation.definitionFit: A prattler chatters idly and childishly, someone who babbles nonsense.

clue.text: One with Japanese skill's new home, German? Yes

parts.note: to be home is to be in

explanation.surface: Asking whether a skilled Japanese person's new home owner is German, and hearing yes.
explanation.definitionFit: Ninjas were warriors trained in the Japanese martial art of ninjutsu, covert fighting and espionage.

clue.text: Not much interested in Westminster or capital oil supply?

indicators.note: read as the adverb of supple, it means flexibly, so the letters bend into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone indifferent to Parliament, or to the oil supplying the capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Supply' is not the noun but supple-ly, flexibly. Westminster is where the UK Parliament sits, so it stands for politics.
explanation.definitionFit: Apolitical people take no interest in politics, and Westminster is the seat of the British government.

clue.text: More tedious originally, include page for island, and do well

indicators.note: putting one thing in for another means one letter is swapped out and another goes in its place

parts.note: prosy means dull, and this is its comparative, as it stands before the change

explanation.surface: A duller original draft gets a page added on an island and succeeds.
explanation.walkthrough: In PROSIER the I is replaced by P.
explanation.definitionFit: To prosper is to flourish or thrive, succeeding financially or otherwise.

clue.text: Agreeable requests followed by worker

parts.note: the worker ant is a crossword staple

explanation.surface: Someone nice makes requests and an employee then follows up.
explanation.definitionFit: Pleasant means pleasing or likeable, so an agreeable thing or person fits.

clue.text: By Italian river somewhere to put food, safe to consume

parts.note: the Po flows across northern Italy
food is set out on a table

explanation.surface: Next to an Italian river there is a place to set down food that is fine to eat.
explanation.definitionFit: Potable describes water or drink that is fit and safe for drinking.

clue.text: Aggressive call before one's retaining company, Eastern

parts.note: to give someone a bell is British slang for phoning them

indicators.note: to retain something is to hold onto it, so one piece is kept inside another

parts.note: one is I, and the possessive adds S

explanation.surface: A hostile phone call precedes someone's firm keeping hold of an Eastern business.
explanation.walkthrough: The possessive in 'one's' supplies a letter of its own, which the company abbreviation then sits before.
explanation.definitionFit: Bellicose means eager to fight, so it is a synonym for hostile and aggressive.

clue.text: It might help to see, briefly, country bird

indicators.note: making something brief cuts it short, here by its final letter

explanation.surface: A briefly glimpsed country bird might aid one's vision.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Briefly' looks like it modifies 'see', but it trims the word after it.
explanation.definitionFit: A lantern is a portable lamp, carried to light the way in the dark.

clue.text: Greek character caught by king referring to power maybe

parts.note: nu is a letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: A Greek figure is captured by a king who speaks of his power.
explanation.definitionFit: Nuclear power is one kind of energy generation, so the adjective can describe power.

clue.text: Lasting long time in Southeast, copper, looked all right from the start

indicators.note: taking things from the start means only each word's opening letter is used

parts.note: first letters of these three words

explanation.surface: A policeman in the South East has looked fine since he began, after long service.
explanation.walkthrough: Copper suggests a police officer but is the metal here.
explanation.definitionFit: Secular can mean lasting for an age or occurring over centuries, as in secular trends.

clue.text: Wonder in bishop's place — first sign of dazzling plants

indicators.note: one piece placed in another sits within it

parts.note: a see is a bishop's diocese

indicators.note: the first sign of a word is its opening letter

explanation.surface: Awe inside a bishop's residence at the first glimpse of brilliant flowers.
explanation.walkthrough: A bishop's see is his diocese, a standard crossword convention.
explanation.definitionFit: Seaweed is a collective name for marine algae, often loosely called sea plants.

clue.text: Lock of hair, very French, brushed in the middle

indicators.note: the middle of a word is its centre, so only the central letter is kept

explanation.surface: A curl of hair, very French, combed in the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: A tress is a long lock or strand of hair, usually in poetic use.

clue.text: Media boss initially irritated by court ruling

indicators.note: initially means at the beginning, so the word gives just its first letter

explanation.surface: A newspaper editor is annoyed by a court judgment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ruling' looks like part of 'court ruling' but stands alone as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An edict is an official order or decree issued by an authority.

clue.text: Adam's son getting regularly slapdash recalled inside — by this person?

definitions.text: Adam's son getting regularly slapdash recalled inside — by this person?

indicators.note: placed inside means set within the other piece

parts.note: Cain, elder son of Adam and Eve in Genesis

indicators.note: to recall is to call back, so the letters run backwards
regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is kept

parts.note: second, fourth, sixth and eighth letters

explanation.surface: Cain, a careless sinner, is called back inside to be counselled by a clergyman.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition: a sinner like Cain might be brought back into the fold by a cleric.
explanation.definitionFit: A chaplain is a clergyman serving an institution, the sort who would try to reclaim a wrongdoer.

clue.text: Ways round English drop in standard

parts.note: laps are circuits of a track

explanation.surface: Running laps round England shows a fall in fitness.
explanation.definitionFit: A lapse is a temporary failure or slip, a falling-off from normal standards.

clue.text: Victor with objective to seek new owner

parts.note: V is Victor in the NATO phonetic alphabet
an end is an aim or objective

explanation.surface: A man named Victor aims to find someone new to own something.
explanation.definitionFit: To vend is to sell, and selling an item means finding it another owner.

clue.text: Church accepting legal claim, note left for customers

indicators.note: accepting something means taking it in, so the other pieces go inside

parts.note: a lien is a legal right over another's property
the seventh note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: The Church takes on a legal claim, leaving a memo for its patrons.
explanation.walkthrough: The Church takes in three pieces at once: the claim, the note and the abbreviation for left.
explanation.definitionFit: Clientele means the body of clients or customers a business serves.

clue.text: Predisposed expert, extremely niche

parts.note: a pro is a professional, an expert

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its two ends, so only first and last letters stay

parts.note: first and last letters of niche

explanation.surface: A specialist inclined toward a highly specialised field.
explanation.definitionFit: Being prone to something means being liable or inclined to it.

clue.text: Recently but not now seen in goal at Everton

indicators.note: something seen in a phrase is visible within its letters

parts.note: the end of goal runs through at into the start of Everton

explanation.surface: A goal scored at Everton's ground was recent news but is old now.
explanation.walkthrough: Everton is a Premier League football club in Liverpool.
explanation.definitionFit: Late can mean recently in existence but now gone, as in the late president.

clue.text: Game boss in advantageous position

explanation.surface: A card game's top player holds the upper hand.
explanation.definitionFit: A bridgehead is a military foothold in enemy territory, from which further advance can be made.
